drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find our proposed revisions for discussion. We have proposed a USD 40,000,000 cash purchase price, clarified closing mechanics, and refined the financial statement representation and indemnity framework. These proposals remain subject to our client's approval and agreement on the complete transaction documents. We welcome your comments.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 40,000,000 (the “Purchase Price”), payable in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the applicable party of the closing conditions expressly set out in this Agreement, or on another date agreed in writing by the parties. At Closing, the Seller shall transfer the Shares against payment of the Purchase Price.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered by the Seller at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements identified in those schedules fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of their respective dates and for their respective periods, in accordance with the accounting principles specified therein, consistently applied, subject, in the case of unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer solely for actual, direct losses arising from a breach of the Seller's express representations or covenants in this Agreement. Claims for breaches of representations must be notified in reasonable detail within twelve months after Closing. The Seller shall have no liability for such claims unless aggregate covered losses exceed one percent of the Purchase Price, and then only for the excess; aggregate liability for such claims shall not exceed ten percent of the Purchase Price. No recovery shall be available to the extent a matter was disclosed in the disclosure schedules, reflected or reserved for in the financial statements, or otherwise recovered, and there shall be no double recovery. Except in cases of fraud by the Seller, this Section shall be the Buyer's exclusive monetary remedy following Closing.

partner.private_reasoning: The rendered agreement and cover note propose USD 40,000,000 and do not disclose the client's confidential minimum acceptable price. No hidden-content categories or other confidential disclosures are identified in the supplied package.

receiver.message_back: Subject to our client’s approval and agreement on definitive documents, Buyer proposes USD 36,000,000, with Closing conditioned on satisfactory diligence, required consents, and the accuracy of Seller’s representations at Closing. We also require complete financial statements prepared consistently under GAAP, disclosure exceptions limited to specifically and fairly disclosed matters, and indemnification for reasonably foreseeable losses with 24-month survival, a 0.5% tipping basket, and a 20% cap, with separate protections outside those limits and the exclusive-remedy restriction for fraud, title, authority, taxes, and covenant breaches.

drafter.private_reasoning: Counter at USD 37,000,000 and offer a balanced indemnity package to narrow the remaining gap. Accommodate GAAP financial reporting and specific disclosure standards while resisting an open-ended diligence condition and uncapped exposure for ordinary covenant breaches. All proposals remain subject to client approval and definitive documentation.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Subject to our client’s approval and agreement on definitive documents, Seller proposes USD 37,000,000. We have revised the draft to accommodate GAAP financial statements, specifically and fairly disclosed exceptions, required consents, and a representation bring-down. Diligence should be completed within a defined period rather than remain an open-ended closing condition. On indemnification, we propose 18-month survival, a 0.75% deductible basket, and a 15% general cap, with separate treatment for title, authority, taxes, and covenants and an exception for Seller’s actual fraud. These concessions are proposed as a package. Please confirm whether this provides a basis to finalize the agreement.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 37,000,000 (the “Purchase Price”), payable in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the party entitled to their benefit of the closing conditions expressly set out in this Agreement, or on another date agreed in writing by the parties. Buyer shall have ten business days after signing to complete its diligence and may terminate during that period by written notice identifying in reasonable detail a material adverse finding concerning the Company. If Buyer does not deliver such notice within that period, the diligence condition shall be deemed satisfied. Buyer's remaining closing conditions shall be receipt of the required third-party and governmental consents specifically identified in this Agreement, Seller's performance of its pre-Closing covenants in all material respects, and the accuracy of Seller's representations at Closing in all material respects (or in all respects where already qualified by materiality), except for representations expressly made as of an earlier date, which shall be tested as of that date. Closing shall not be subject to a financing condition. At Closing, the Seller shall transfer the Shares against payment of the Purchase Price.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except for matters specifically and fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered by the Seller at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements identified in those schedules are complete in all material respects and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of their respective dates and for their respective periods, in accordance with GAAP consistently applied, subject, solely in the case of unaudited interim statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes. Each disclosure shall identify the nature and scope of the exception with sufficient detail to permit a reasonable buyer to understand it and shall qualify only the representation to which it expressly relates and any other representation to which its relevance is reasonably apparent on its face.

4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual losses reasonably foreseeable as a result of a breach of the Seller's express representations or covenants in this Agreement. Punitive or exemplary damages shall be excluded except to the extent payable to a third party under a covered claim. Claims for breaches of representations must be notified in reasonable detail within eighteen months after Closing; timely notified claims shall survive until finally resolved. Except as provided below, Seller shall have no liability for representation claims unless aggregate covered losses exceed 0.75% of the Purchase Price, and then only for the excess, and aggregate liability for such claims shall not exceed 15% of the Purchase Price. Claims concerning Seller's title to the Shares or authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and claims under the tax indemnity, shall not be subject to that basket or general cap and shall survive until sixty days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for unpaid taxes of the Company attributable to periods ending on or before Closing and the pre-Closing portion of any straddle period, except to the extent specifically reflected in the final purchase price calculation. Covenant claims shall not be subject to the basket or general cap; pre-Closing covenant claims must be notified within eighteen months after Closing, and post-Closing covenant claims within twelve months after the applicable performance obligation expires. Seller's aggregate liability under this Agreement, including these special claims, shall not exceed the Purchase Price, except for Seller's actual fraud. No recovery shall be available to the extent a matter was specifically and fairly disclosed in accordance with Section 3, specifically reflected or reserved for in the financial statements, or otherwise recovered, and there shall be no double recovery; disclosure shall not excuse performance of an express covenant or payment under the tax indemnity. Buyer shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate covered losses. Except for Seller's actual fraud and claims for equitable relief to enforce express covenants, this Section shall be Buyer's exclusive remedy following Closing, including for title, authority, tax, and covenant claims. Nothing in this Section limits liability for Seller's actual fraud.

receiver.message_back: Subject to Buyer’s approval and definitive documentation, we can proceed at USD 37,000,000 with the proposed 18-month survival, 0.75% deductible basket and 15% general cap, provided the ten-business-day diligence period begins only upon delivery of complete schedules and reasonably requested diligence materials, all required closing consents are expressly listed, and Seller’s title and authority representations are brought down without a materiality qualifier. We also require removal of the foreseeability limitation on indemnifiable losses and that financial-statement reserves reduce recovery only to the extent actually credited in the purchase price; the proposed separate treatment of title, authority, taxes, covenants and Seller’s actual fraud otherwise provides a basis to finalize.
